sentences.text: This appeal is preferred by the appellants/claimants aggrieved by the judgment and decree dated 18.07.2018 passed in M.V.O.P.No.137 of 2017 by the Chairman, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-II Additional District Judge (FTC), Mancherial, whereby compensation of Rs.26,40,500/- was awarded for the death of one Chintakindi Vijaya (hereinafter referred to as "the deceased") in a motor vehicle accident.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-II Additional District Judge (FTC), Mancherial
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The brief facts of the case are that on 09.05.2016 at about 5.30 pm, while the deceased was travelling in a bus bearing No.TS-09-UA- 5026, the driver drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner, due to which the bus turned turtle and fell into a valley, resulting in the death of the deceased at the spot.

The appellants/claimants, being the sons and daughter of the deceased, filed the aforesaid claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act before the Tribunal claiming compensation of Rs.40,38,000/- for her death in a road accident.

The Tribunal, upon appreciation of evidence, held that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and awarded compensation of Rs.26,40,500/- with interest at 9% per annum.
Aggrieved thereby, the appellants/claimants filed the present appeal seeking enhancement of compensation.

3. Learned counsel for the appellants contended that the Tribunal erred in adopting appropriate multiplier and also failed to properly consider the income of the deceased based on salary certificates.
Learned counsel further contended that the amounts awarded under conventional heads are contrary to settled principles of law and hence prayed for enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned Standing Counsel appearing for respondent No.3-Insurance Company supported the award passed by the Tribunal.
5. There is no dispute with regard to the occurrence of the accident or the finding of negligence recorded by the Tribunal.
The same has attained finality.

6. So far as the quantum of compensation is concerned, with regard to the income of the deceased,
the Tribunal has rightly taken into consideration the salary certificates (Exs.A6 to A17) and assessed the annual income at Rs.5,70,062/- after deduction of income tax.
The said finding is based on cogent evidence and requires no interference.

Further, considering that the deceased was aged 58 years at the time of the accident, the appropriate multiplier applicable, as per the settled principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, is '9'.
Therefore, the multiplier adopted by the Tribunal is correct and calls for no interference.

Coming to the deduction towards personal expenses, the Tribunal observed that the claimants are majors and not dependent on the income of the deceased and accordingly deducted 50% of the income towards personal expenses.
The said approach is in consonance with the settled legal principles.
Thus, the amount awarded by the Tribunal towards loss of dependency at Rs.25,65,279/- is confirmed.
The Tribunal has further awarded a sum of Rs.25,000/- towards pain and agony, which appears to be just and reasonable, and the same is accordingly affirmed.

However, insofar as the amounts awarded under conventional heads are concerned, the Tribunal granted only Rs.25,000/- each towards funeral expenses and loss of estate,
which are on the lower side.

In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi 1, the appellants-claimants are entitled to Rs.91,000/-
(Rs.70,000/- + 10% enhancement for every three years) under the conventional heads.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Accordingly,
the compensation under the said heads is enhanced to Rs.91,000/-.

Thus, the total compensation payable to the appellants- claimants is recalculated as Rs.26,81,279/- (Rs.25,65,279/- + Rs.25,000/-
+ Rs.91,000/-), which is rounded off to Rs.26,81,000/-.
7. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed enhancing the compensation awarded by the Tribunal from Rs.26,40,500/- to Rs.26,81,000/-.
The enhanced compensation amount shall carry interest at 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
The remaining terms and conditions of the Tribunal shall stand unaltered.
No order as to costs.
As a sequel, the miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
